label: Resilient Well-Connected Graduate Woman
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below typical thresholds, near-minimal depression on the PHQ-9, and virtually negligible anxiety on the GAD-7. The combination of low scores across all three distress dimensions suggests a stable, emotionally resilient group with strong social connectedness.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social media use
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness, indicating robust social connections and sense of belonging
Exhibits near-floor depressive symptom levels, suggesting positive mood regulation
Displays virtually no anxiety symptoms, reflecting emotional stability
Maintains moderate screen or social media use (1–3 hours), suggesting balanced digital engagement
Highly educated, which may contribute to access to coping resources and social support networks

label: High-Distress Heavy-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures respondents who report elevated loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms relative to other groups. They are predominantly female with graduate-level education and spend more than five hours daily on digital devices or online platforms. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean ≈ 1.67), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean ≈ 1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean ≈ 2.16) all sit in the higher range, indicating a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress across all three dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/online usage exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Scores notably high on GAD-7 anxiety items, the most pronounced distress indicator in this profile
Engages in heavy daily digital or online usage (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounded psychological burden
tone: Distressed and emotionally burdened, reflecting a convergence of loneliness, depressive mood, and anxious affect

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.23, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.80, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating generally robust mental well-being.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, spending 1–3 hours of daily screen/online time
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology, well below clinical concern
Demonstrates low anxiety levels consistent with healthy psychological functioning
Maintains moderate daily screen or online usage (1–3 hours), suggesting balanced digital habits
Belongs to a relatively large respondent cluster (n=341), indicating this is a common well-being pattern in the sample
tone: Stable, emotionally grounded, and psychologically resilient
